name: Bukat
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description is only a 15pp wordlist (Roth 1896); no grammar or phonology of Bukat located

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard & Antonia Soriente. 2015. The languages and peoples of the Müller Mountains: A contribution to the study of the origins of Borneo's nomads and their languages. Wacana 16(2): 339-354. doi:10.17510/wacana.v16i2.381
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Only first-hand Bukat phonological material found anywhere: Table 4 'Bukat consonants' (p. 347), geminates -ll-/-tt-, no consonant clusters, 6 phonemic vowels (Table 6, p. 348). Nothing on Bukat stress; the article's single stress remark is about Seputan ('its strong stress on the penultimate syllable', p. 344).

sources.citation: Blust, Robert & Alexander D. Smith. 2014. A bibliography of the languages of Borneo (and Madagascar). Phillips, ME: Borneo Research Council.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'Bukat (Kayanic?; Kalimantan; 400 in 1981)'; the only work indexed under Bukat is King 1974 (keyword 'other'). No descriptive or phonological work on Bukat is listed.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. 723 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: 'Bukat' occurs only twice: in the classification list (Müller-Schwaner Punan: Aoheng, Bukat, Hovongan, Kereho, Punan Aput, Punan Merah; p. 37) and in the bibliography (King 1974). No Bukat data; nothing on Bukat stress.

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard. 1981. Three-gender personal pronouns in some languages of central Borneo. Borneo Research Bulletin 13(1): 48-49.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pronoun note on the MSP languages (Seputan, Kereho, Nanga Ira', Aoheng); Bukat named only as 'the Bukat group (which includes Bukat, Punan-Merah and Punan-Lisum)'. No Bukat data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: King, Victor. 1974. Notes on Punan and Bukat in West Kalimantan. Borneo Research Bulletin 6(2): 39-42.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic field note (villages, economy, access); only linguistic sentence: 'The Bukat and Punan are linguistically and culturally distinct, as are the Penihing.' No wordlist, no phonology, nothing on stress. This is the only Bukat item in Blust & Smith 2014.

sources.citation: Roth, Henry Ling. 1896. The natives of Sarawak and British North Borneo, vol. 2. London: Truslove & Hanson.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog attaches this to bvk as a wordlist, but the appendix vocabulary column is 'Bukutan' (= Bukitan [bkn]); a full-text search for stress/accent Bukat/Bukut/Bhuket finds no Bukat material and no stress remark.
Classification and speaker count only (400 in 1981, Wurm & Hattori); no phonology; cite only Ethnologue/Glottolog.

sources.citation: Antonia Soriente, unpublished Bukat wordlist/field data underlying Sellato & Soriente 2015 Table 4
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 2015 consonant table implies elicited Bukat data exist; a fuller phonological sketch by Soriente (Naples L'Orientale) would be the first source to state stress.

sources.citation: Thambiah, Shanthi. 1995. Culture as adaptation: Change among the Bhuket of Sarawak, Malaysia. PhD thesis, University of Hull. 236 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only monograph-length study of the Sarawak (Bhuket) side; may include a note on the language/orthography.

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard. 1994. Nomads of the Borneo rainforest: The economics, politics, and ideology of settling down. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press (transl. of Sellato 1989, Nomades et sédentarisation à Bornéo, EHESS).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Main monograph on the Bukat by the one scholar who collected Bukat language data; may contain a language note or wordlist with orthographic stress marks; Glottolog's fullest Bukat reference.

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard. 1987. Les nomades forestiers de Bornéo et la sédentarisation: essai d'histoire économique et sociale. Thèse de doctorat, EHESS Paris. 570 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: 570-page thesis version (vs 293-page 1989 book) of the same work; the most likely place for Sellato's raw Bukat linguistic notes/wordlists.

sources.citation: Rousseau, Jérôme. 1971. [Bukat/Bhuket] fieldnotes (unpublished; listed by Glottolog).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Unpublished field material on Balui Bhuket from the Kayan ethnographer; would be the only Sarawak-side linguistic notes.
